key_insight: A physics-tailored deep learning surrogate can replace expensive electromagnetic simulations for inverse-designing very large free-form metasurfaces while preserving nanoscale design freedom.
engineering_relevance: This enables gradient-based topology optimization of system-scale photonic devices, making practical designs such as wide-angle metagratings and large holographic metasurfaces computationally feasible.
method: Trains a deep-learning surrogate on small-scale electromagnetic simulations.
Uses locality and symmetry priors to generalize to metasurfaces orders of magnitude larger.
Performs gradient-based inverse design under arbitrary illumination while capturing nonlocal interactions.
evidence_signal: The model predicts optical fields more than four orders of magnitude faster than the conventional solver and was validated on metagratings up to 75° diffraction plus a >1,000-wavelength, 1.6-billion-DOF holographic metasurface.
watch_item: Performance depends on the surrogate faithfully covering the relevant design space and physical conditions; out-of-distribution geometries or illumination settings may require retraining or careful validation.
paper_title: Deep learning enables large-scale inverse design of free-form metasurfaces
